Task: update ONLY src/core/types.ts to contract v1. Do not touch any other file. Never read .env or print environment variables. No network calls, no new dependencies. snake_case everywhere.

Changes:
1. Remove Evidence and EvidenceStatus. Add:
   - type FactStatus = "given" | "extracted" | "cross_checked" | "uncertain"
   - type FactProvider = "crustdata" | "fixture" | "user_input" | "derived" | "model"
   - interface FactSource { provider: FactProvider; operation?: "autocomplete" | "company_search" | "company_enrich"; record_id?: string; retrieved_at: string; source_url?: string }
   - interface Fact<T> { id: string; value: T; claim: string; field?: string; source: FactSource; status: FactStatus; as_of?: string; derived_from?: readonly string[] }
   - type AnyFact = Fact<unknown>
   - export const CITEABLE_FACT_STATUSES: readonly FactStatus[] = ["given", "cross_checked"]
   All readonly. Comment each status precisely: given = reported directly by a provider or the user, unchanged; extracted = pulled out of free text, not citeable until verified; cross_checked = at least two independent facts agree and are listed in derived_from; uncertain = conflicting or unsupported, never citeable. Comment that only deterministic code sets status, the model may only reference existing fact ids, and facts with provider "model" are never citeable.
2. Prospect gets facts: readonly AnyFact[]. Assessment no longer holds evidence items; CriterionScore.evidence_ids becomes fact_ids; OutreachDraft.cited_evidence_ids becomes cited_fact_ids.
3. RunStep gets "plan" in addition to search, validate, enrich, assess. Run counts gain llm_calls, llm_input_tokens, llm_output_tokens.
4. RunConfig gains: model (string), max_llm_calls_per_run (number), max_output_tokens_per_call (number). DEFAULT_RUN_CONFIG: model "claude-haiku", max_llm_calls_per_run 20, max_output_tokens_per_call 1500 (starting values to tune; say so in a comment), keeping the 100 and 15 caps. Add DEV_RUN_CONFIG: max_search_results 10, max_enrichments 2, same model and LLM caps.
5. Update every comment that mentions the old names.

Then run npx tsc --noEmit and npx vitest run (existing tests must still pass). Summarise in 6 bullets what changed and anything you were unsure about.

`src/core/types.ts` is now on contract v1. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and `npx vitest run` passes 18 of 18. I touched no other file.

- **Facts replace evidence:** I removed `Evidence` and `EvidenceStatus`. I added `FactStatus`, `FactProvider`, `FactSource`, `Fact<T>`, `AnyFact` and `CITEABLE_FACT_STATUSES` (`given` and `cross_checked`), all readonly. Each status is commented as you specified. A header comment says only deterministic code sets status, the model may only reference existing fact ids, and `model`-provider facts are never citeable.
- **Prospect and Assessment:** `Prospect` now has `facts: readonly AnyFact[]`. `Assessment` no longer holds evidence items. `CriterionScore.evidence_ids` is now `fact_ids`, and `OutreachDraft.cited_evidence_ids` is now `cited_fact_ids`. No mention of the old names remains in the file.
- **Run steps and counts:** `RunStep` gains `"plan"`, which also adds it to the `RunCosts` and `RunTimings` keys. `RunCounts` gains `llm_calls`, `llm_input_tokens` and `llm_output_tokens`.
- **Config:** `RunConfig` gains `model`, `max_llm_calls_per_run` and `max_output_tokens_per_call`. `DEFAULT_RUN_CONFIG` uses `"claude-haiku"`, 20 and 1500, keeps the 100 and 15 caps, and has a comment saying the model and LLM caps are starting values to tune. `DEV_RUN_CONFIG` uses 10 search results, 2 enrichments and the same model and LLM caps.
- **Unsure, `Prospect.facts`:** I made it required, as you wrote it. Code that builds a `Prospect` before enrichment will need to pass `[]`. No existing code broke, but later code will hit this.
- **Unsure, comments:** I edited the `OutreachDraft` rule to say it may only cite facts in `CITEABLE_FACT_STATUSES` whose provider isn't `"model"`. I also reworded the `Assessment.outreach` comment to "citeable fact".

Task: create the provider interface and the fixture provider. Create ONLY src/core/data/provider.ts, src/core/data/fixture-provider.ts and tests/fixture-provider.test.ts. Do not edit other files. Never read .env or print environment variables. No network calls, no new dependencies, no Next.js or neatlogs imports. Read src/core/types.ts and src/core/fixtures/companies.ts first.

provider.ts: export interface CompanyProvider with three async methods:
- autocompleteIndustry(query: string): Promise<ProviderResult<readonly string[]>>
- searchCompanies(filters: SearchFilters, limit: number): Promise<ProviderResult<readonly RawCompany[]>>
- enrichCompanies(linkedin_urls: readonly string[]): Promise<ProviderResult<readonly RawCompany[]>>
ProviderResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T; cost_usd: number; calls: number } | { ok: false; error: ProviderError }. ProviderError has a category: "auth_failed" | "rate_limited" | "timeout" | "bad_request" | "no_match" | "budget_cap_reached" | "empty_or_partial" and a message. SearchFilters: country (string), industries (readonly string[]), employee_count_ranges (readonly string[]). Also export class BudgetGuard, constructed from RunConfig (max_search_results, max_enrichments), with canSearch(limit), canEnrich(count), recordSearch(n, cost), recordEnrich(n, cost) and snapshot() returning spent cost and counts. canSearch and canEnrich return false when a cap would be exceeded, and providers must return budget_cap_reached instead of making the call.

fixture-provider.ts: class FixtureProvider implements CompanyProvider, using the synthetic fixtures, deterministic, cost_usd 0 by default but configurable per call so tests can simulate cost, using a BudgetGuard, and with optional failure injection (for example fail the Nth call with a given error category) so we can demonstrate recovery. enrichCompanies returns fixture records whose LinkedIn URL matches and returns no_match for the rest.

Tests: caps respected, failure injection works, no_match for unknown URLs.

Run npx vitest run and npx tsc --noEmit. Summarise in 6 bullets, including anything you were unsure about.

content.text:
I added `src/core/data/provider.ts`, `src/core/data/fixture-provider.ts` and `tests/fixture-provider.test.ts`, and edited no other file. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and `npx vitest run` passes 27 of 27, including 9 new tests.

- **Interface:** `provider.ts` has `CompanyProvider`, `ProviderResult<T>`, `ProviderError` with the seven categories, and `SearchFilters`. `BudgetGuard` takes `max_search_results` and `max_enrichments`. Its `canSearch` and `canEnrich` return false when a cap would be exceeded, and `recordSearch`, `recordEnrich` and `snapshot()` work as specified.
- **Fixture provider:**
  - `FixtureProvider` is deterministic and makes no network calls. It returns `budget_cap_reached` before counting a call or touching any data.
  - Cost is 0 unless you pass `cost_usd` as a number or a function of the call number.
  - Failure injection is `failures: [{ call_number, category, message? }]`. The call number is 1-based and counts every call across all three methods, including failed ones.
  - It also exposes `calls_made` and `budget`.
- **Enrich:** URLs are matched after `normalizeLinkedInUrl`, so case and trailing-slash differences still match. If no URL matches, it returns `no_match`.
- **Unsure, partial enrich:** If only some URLs match, it returns `ok` with the matched records, and the unmatched URLs are simply absent. The result type can't carry both data and an error. Say if you'd rather have `empty_or_partial`.
- **Unsure, cap accounting:**
  - Search checks the requested `limit` against the cap, but records only the number of companies actually returned.
  - Enrich checks the number of URLs requested, but records only the number matched.
  - Autocomplete is free and outside both caps.
  - A failed or `no_match` call records no spend, but it still counts toward the injected call number.
- **Unsure, search filters:**
  - Industries match case-insensitively. Employee ranges match exactly.
  - The country filter applies only to records that have a `location.country`. The fixtures mostly have none, so those pass.
  - Search results are relabeled `source: "search"`, while the fixture records themselves stay as they are.
